Commentary.Commentary: This morning again, he started from one end and kept the fire going. The pitch helped him as he picked the wicket of Agarwal with one that kept low and got to his fifth. Then, bounced out Jadeja with a snorter of a ball. The last one to fall was Pant who was caught behind off a Hazlewood delivery. The Indians will not mind this too much as they got what they came for and scored the runs they think they require. Now onto the chase, then. Not going to be easy for the hosts. They will hope it starts to rain soon. The final innings will start shortly.

And with that dismissal, Virat Kohli calls his batsmen off and India have declared on 106/8. That means AUSTRALIA NEED 399 TO WIN! A quick moving hour of play this morning. The Indians came out playing their shots and eventually lost wickets as well. It didn't matter that much as they added 52 runs to their overnight lead. The Indian second innings was about Mayank Agarwal again as the opener scored a good-looking 42 to follow up his 76 in the first dig. But more than him, the second innings was about Pat Cummins who picked up six wickets, in fact his best Test figures of 6/27. 4 of them came the previous evening where he had the two best Indian batsmen out for ducks.

OUT! Pant departs looking to score off an innovative stroke. Hazlewood bangs it short on middle and leg, Pant makes room, looks to ramp it over the keeper's head but can get it only as far as Paine behind. Simple take for him.

SIX! BANG! Take that, Josh Hazlewood. Shows him no mercy. Wow. The big pacer comes from around the wicket and fires it full outside off, Rishabh Pant just throws everything behind this and bludgeons it straight back over the bowler's head for a maximum. Amazing hit.
Angling away from a fuller length, left alone.
Short outside off again, Shami does well to get on top of the bounce and fends it off towards point.

NOT OUT! Shami survives and Cummins will have to try again for his seventh. Short length ball again just down the leg side, the Indian pacer tries to pull this but misses the ball. It is mighty close to the bat and Paine collects the ball behind. There is not a big appeal but the bowler seems a little interested and the Aussie skipper goes upstairs eventually. Replays roll in and show that there is no bat involved and the on-field umpire can remain with his original decision of not out. Australia have lost a review here. But one has to applaud the way Cummins is running in and bowling with fire every ball.
Review taken by Australia. It's for a caught behind decision against Mohammed Shami.
Bouncer going down the leg side, Shami tries to pull it but cannot connect this ball.
Mohammed Shami is in at number 9, replacing Ravindra Jadeja.

OUT! Bounced him out! Cummins has six! Might not be very important in the context of the game but mighty a good performance from the quick. The previous ball was well outside off but this bouncer is aimed at the body and immediately, Jadeja is uncomfortable. He tries to fend it off on the leg side but the ball lobs off the glove and flies towards Usman Khawaja at gully who comes ahead and takes this catch. Cummins had bowled beautifully yesterday and today as well. India are effectively 392/7 now.
FOUR! Shot! Short-arm jab over mid-wicket and all the way for a boundary. Short of a length ball outside off, Jadeja pulls this in front of square on the leg side and holds his pose for the cameras.
It's got dark out there, so the floodlights have been switched on. Rain could be around the corner, so you'd have to wonder if the declaration is as well.

Short length ball outside off, keeps a little low again. Pant tries to pull this one but only gets a thick inside edge that goes onto his pads. Lucky that didn't go on the stumps. Single taken as the ball just drops on the pitch.
Jadeja stays inside the crease and keeps it out without much trouble.
Outside off on a good length, it's tapped just wide of the cover fielder for a quick run.
Banged in short, Pant takes the pull shot on but fails to connect.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
What was that? A wild swing from Jadeja as Hazlewood throws it wide outside off, it keeps low and Paine has an uneven bounce in front of him. He can't collect cleanly and a bye is taken.
Short of a good length outside off, punched off the back foot through the covers for a single.
Pant does eventually get to the other end. Length ball on the pads, Pant turns it down on the leg side for a single to fine leg.

Wide! Signaled for bowling this well down the leg side and possibly, deliberately to keep Pant off strike. Length ball way down the leg side, so far down that Pant cannot get bat on it. Tim Paine collects it and tries to get to the other end for the next over but Marais Erasmus is quick to spot this and signals it as wide. He is not going to allow the Aussies to get away with that, as they tried to be too negative. The Aussie skipper is not convinced by the decision and goes to have a chat with the umpire but the latter tells him that the decision will stand and the reason for it. Cummins will have to bowl another one.
Bouncer to Pant! The Indian keeper ducks under the ball and lets it go.
Shorter delivery to Jadeja, the left-hander goes for the pull. It is in the air but just drops short of Marcus Harris in the deep square leg position. The boundary is huge there. Single taken.
Fuller this time, and another good-looking shot but just for a single through the covers. Pant timed that cover drive really well but there was Starc at wide mid off to stop it.

FOUR! Stand and deliver stuff from Rishabh Pant. Produces these brilliant shots every now and then. This ball is on a shorter length outside off, Pant stands tall and punches this one off the back foot through cover and the ball reaches the fence. Deep point cannot come around in time to stop it.
Length ball, Pant pushes it right back to the bowler.
Nasty from Hazlewood. He bangs it in short and hard and it's an accurate one, Jadeja awkwardly fends it down in front of the slip cordon. Nicely done from the batsman.
In line with the stumps this time, worked down in front of short mid-wicket. Both batsmen take off and complete the run with ease.
Too far outside off again, it is left alone.
Full and wide outside off, Pant has nothing to do with that one.
Angling away from the left-hander, slightly fuller in length, Pant pushes away from his body and finds the cover fielder.
Full length delivery attacking the off stump, Pant drives but can't beat mid off.
Ravindra Jadeja in at number 8, replacing Mayank Agarwal. Also, Josh Hazlewood to replace Nathan Lyon.

OUT! Bowled 'em! The ball has snuck through and disturbed the timber. Fifer for Pat Cummins, 3rd of his Test career. No consecutive fifties for Agarwal as he departs for 42. The ball has kept low once again and Mayank, who is in two minds due to the pitch misbehaving in this over, plays this one back in the crease. The short of a length ball on off does not rise enough and the opener, who tries to put his bat down and prevent the ball from going on to hit his stumps, cannot do so. The ball goes off the bottom half and disturbs the off stump. Well batted from Agarwal but not much one could do there. But take nothing away from Cummins, he has bowled exceptionally well here and deserved this 5-wicket haul. Has run in hard every single ball.
Fuller length ball and Agarwal is playing back to this one. Does well again to bring his bat down in time and keep it out.
A length ball that behaves normally and Agarwal stands tall and defends.

What is happening to the pitch? One rears up and seams wildly and the next one keeps incredibly low from a length. Agarwal does well to bring his bat down in time and the ball goes off the outside edge towards first slip. Tough batting here.

FOUR BYES! That has gone through everything. Pacy and incredible movement after landing, must have hit a crack or something on the wicket. The deviation is huge after landing on off and middle. Agarwal who is looking to drive this uppishly back down the ground is beaten between his bat and pad and the ball misses his leg stump due to the ball seaming and bouncing. Paine too, can't get a hand on it and the ball runs away for four byes.
Around the wicket, slower short ball outside off. Pant drops the ball towards mid off and runs through for a quick single.
Really quick, at 98.4 kph from the off-spinner. Agarwal comes ahead and defends it.
Another ball on the pads, another flick but no run available.
Flatter ball on the pads to Agarwal, worked away on the leg side.
Slightly slower outside off, the Indian wicket-keeper batsman pushes it on the off side for a single.
FOUR! Short and wide, Rishabh Pant cuts this really late and fine to beat Pat Cummins at backward point. The ball runs all the way to the fence, with the pace on the ball.
Quicker delivery outside off, left alone by Pant.
Goes full this time, just outside off, the batsman is forward as he pushes it a bit square towards cover-point.
Just behind a length and around off, Mayank shows the full face of the bat and keeps it out from the back foot.
Bumper from Cummins, Agarwal ducks and evades.
Almost a replica of the previous delivery. Cuts back in from a length and catches Mayank Agarwal high on the thigh pad. No appeal on this occasion.

Sharp delivery from Pat Cummins. He's been Australia's best bowler by a distance, is continuing to show that even now. Serves it on a length on middle and it jags back in, Agarwal is beaten and is caught on the thigh pad. An appeal for lbw goes up, but height is an issue.
Length delivery angling back in, goes down leg in fact as Agarwal misses his flick.
Another flatter ball on middle and off to end the over, Pant is on his back foot as he defensively pushes it back. 14 runs off the over, a great one for the Indians.
Flatter ball, quicker in response to the two big shots. Agarwal flicks it away on the leg side for a single and gets to the other end.

SIX! The second maximum of the over! Lyon isn't used to this, at least not so far in this series. Another looped up ball on middle, Agarwal comes down the track again and just times this one with a brilliant straight-bat loft over the bowler's head. The ball goes all the way and hits the sightscreen. Real good batting this, showing people how to play the wily off spinner.
Flatter ball on the pads, pushed towards the leg side with soft hands.

SIX! It's huge! Looped outside off and Agarwal has his dancing shoes on as he comes down the track and lifts it over long off for a biggie. Lovely shot, especially against the turn. Looks like Mayank has come out with a set plan.
Flatter ball on off, Pant stands tall and pushes it to long on for a single.
A front foot defensive stroke from Mayank to end the over.
Length ball slightly angling in, pushed towards mid-wicket.
Length delivery on off, driven back down the ground by Agarwal.
Over the wicket, shorter length outside off. Pushed towards cover for a single. The 350-run lead up for the visitors.

DROPPED! Cummins could have had his fifth but Paine can't quite hold on. The ball came in after landing on a length outside off from around the wicket. Pant tried to push at the ball but got an inside edge that carried to Paine. He dived to his right to take this one but couldn't hold on. The ball rolls towards the fence where Mitchell Marsh makes a good stop and saves a couple of runs for his team.
Wide outside off, left alone by the Indian wicket-keeper batsman.
Pat Cummins to bowl from the other end. 4/10 so far off his 6 overs.
Looped up outside off, Agarwal comes ahead and dead-bats.
Flatter ball on middle, nudged towards mid-wicket and Pant gets to the other end.
This one goes straight on and Rishabh is ahead to defend.

Oooh! that would excite Jadeja as well. The ball gripped and turned and bounced as well. Landed on off with some loop, the ball turns a long way to beat the outside edge of Pant's bat as he comes ahead to defend.
Flatter one on middle, Pant comes ahead to keep it out.
First run of the day on the first ball, fuller and quicker on middle and pushed down to long on for a single by Agarwal.

The players and umpires have made their way onto the ground. Nathan Lyon to begin proceedings and Mayank Agarwal will take strike for India, Rishabh Pant at the non-striker's end. The umpire says 'Play' and here we go!

So, then, Day 4 should be an amazing watch, if we are allowed to have some uninterrupted action that is. There is a 60 percent rain forecast for the day and it has been raining on and off causing the groundstaff to bring on the covers and take them off in a cat and mouse type way. Intermittent thunderstorms are predicted for the day and all we can do is hope for them to stay away so we can have some good cricket. Although, these rains might come to help Australia to remove some time out of the game and try for a draw. But if it doesn't rain and we do have a normal game, then India would like to score some quick runs from the bats of mainly Mayank Agarwal, Rishabh Pant and Ravindra Jadeja. The aim will be to set a target that is too high for the hosts to achieve while trying to make them bat soon so that they can have enough time to pick 10 wickets too. The action is not far away.

Welcome to Day 4! What a magnificent day the third one was. After two slow days, Day 3 was just what this Test needed to come to life and boy, did it spring to life or what? Never mind what team's supporter you are, what you want to see is tough Test cricket and a great battle between bat and ball. 15 wickets fell, India decided they did not want to bat fourth for some reason, Australia reduced the visitors to 54/5 by the end of the day to remain valid in the game. What did the game not have? Wonderful for viewership and the Test is back alive, but one would have to believe that despite their poor start in the 2nd innings, India do hold the cards in the game with the 346-run lead they have currently.
... Fourth Day, Morning Session ...

India are 54/5, and they lead by 346 runs, but this Test just got that little bit more interesting. The away side is still in the driver's seat, but the Kangaroos will be in better spirits come Day 4. One more thing that could play in their favour is the fact that there is rain forecast for the remaining two days, which could help and dent hopes, depending on which side you lean towards. It'll be intriguing to see how this all unfolds. The action from Day 4 begins at 1030 local (2330 GMT, previous day). Do join in for all the action. Take care!

It all began with India wrapping up the Australians in the final session with Jasprit Bumrah leading the charge with a 6-fer. The others too did their part, with everyone barring Vihari sharing the wickets. The visitors had a massive lead of 292, and they chose to bat again instead of enforcing the follow-on. At this point everyone thought they would run away with the game, but up rose a warrior in the form of Pat Cummins and he decimated the Indian top order claiming 4 wickets in 4 overs, while Hazlewood took the remaining one.

Finally, a session in Australia's favour, though it's still only a small victory in the larger context of the game. It's been an entertaining day of cricket, wherein 197 runs were scored and 15 wickets scalped. In this final session alone, 60 came of those 197 and 8 from those 15. Those numbers should indicate what a fun day of Test cricket it's been.

Some drama on the last ball of the day. Hazlewood fires it full on leg, it catches Agarwal low on his pads as he looks to tickle it fine. It goes down the leg side and a loud appeal goes up. Nothing from the umpire. The batsmen cross and it's a leg bye. STUMPS ON DAY 3!
Tim Paine is getting creative with his field here. Has a short leg, silly point in place, along with a modified backward square leg who's a bit finer.
Short of a good length into the body, Pant helps the pull, this time through backward square leg. Just the single on this occasion.
Yorker fired in on off, Rishabh brings his bat down and plays it off the inner half towards mid-wicket.

FOUR! Not as short on this occasion, it's shortish and down the leg side. Pant is in complete control of this one as he helps the pull across the fine leg fence. The 50 is up for India. They lead by 344.
Short and a bit down the leg side, the southpaw looks to pull but then opts out of it.
Another accurate bouncer from Hazlewood, he's generating some serious pace and bounce off this deck. Bangs it in short on middle and leg and Pant is beaten as he looks to pull.
Sees the flight on the ball, comes down the track and then knocks it to long off for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Positions himself well behind the line and defends it back down the track.
Uses the depth of the crease to go back and keep it out with a straight blade.
Landing on off, some drift in and then turns away, Pant defends it well.
From around the wicket, it's floated around off, Pant comes forward and blocks it out.
And Mayank Agarwal is receiving medical treatment after he copped a blow on his hand. The magic spray is out and it does its job. The opener is fine to continue.
Another nasty bouncer from Hazlewood. Bangs it in hard on off, Agarwal somehow, barely and awkwardly manages to fend it down off his glove.
Full in length, at the base of off stump, drilled but straight to the man at cover.
Sharp bumper on middle and off, the batsman just arches back and ducks under it. Well done, as the bumper was sharp and accurate.
Fuller in length, attacking the stumps this time, the opener brings a straight bat down in defense.
Outside off again, on a back of a length this time, punched off the back foot straight to short cover.
Good length delivery in the channel outside off, it's defended from inside the crease.
Short and flat outside off, cut down towards third man for three good runs.
Lbw appeal, shut down. Flat, short and spinning down, Agarwal gets low to help the sweep behind square leg but is caught on the pad. It's going down leg clearly.
Turns in from outside off, Mayank stays behind the line and defends it with a straight bat.
Goes deep inside the crease and turns it to backward square leg.
Spinning in on middle and leg, worked down in front of square leg.
Spinning in from outside off, Agarwal backs away and cuts it square, straight to point though.
Bouncer on middle and leg, Pant just about manages to duck under it.
Rishabh Pant walks out to bat next.

OUT! Edged and gone! Half the Indian side is back in the dressing room now. A twist left in this tale? May very well be. Short of a length outside off and there's some extra bounce on this too, which gets Rohit Sharma. He looks to cut but edges it behind due to the extra bounce. It's a simple catch for Shaun Marsh at first slip. India lead by 336 runs.
The batsman has punched that ball through the off side.
Hazlewood generates some extra bounce again, lands it around off and Sharma rises on his toes to defend this away.
On a good length once more, just outside off, Sharma keeps it out with a straight bat.
Rising from a good length, it's just outside off, Sharma keeps it out well from inside his crease.
Josh Hazlewood is into the attack.
Mayank Agarwal has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Loud shout... denied. And while this is going down, the batsmen sneakily pinch a run. Tossed up outside off, turns in, Rohit prods forward to defend but it goes off the inside edge, lobs off the pads and falls on the off side. Everybody is busy appealing and the batsmen use this opportunity to cross over.
Goes with the spin and works it down on the leg side.
Quite full in length and around off, once more the batsman is well forward in defense.
Tossed up off spinner outside off, comes in and Rohit plays it from the front foot.
In the air for a bit but Rohit is safe. Tries to get close to the pitch but isn't exactly able to do so. It turns and goes off the inner half past short leg.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman. That will be the end of the over.
Shortish delivery just outside off, the batsman rises and taps it down on the off side.
Length delivery quite close to off, it's kept out safely from within the crease.
Well timed. Cummins brings it back in on middle and leg, Mayank tucks this behind square on the leg side and manages to come back for the second.
Shaping back in on middle and leg, worked down on the leg side with gentle hands.
Edged and FOUR! Cummins is a bit unlucky. Length ball outside off with some extra bounce, takes the outside edge of Agarwal's hanging bat and runs past the slip cordon for a boundary.
Extremely full on middle and leg, flicked straight to the man at short mid-wicket.
Full and wide outside off, it's driven square through point for a single.
Easily done. Rohit Sharma steps out of his crease and wrists it with the spin to long on. Crosses over to complete the run.
Tossed up off break, on the stumps, it's pushed straight back down to the bowler.
Skips down the track, gets close to the pitch of the floated ball and turns it to mid on.
Serves it well outside off, turns in as Rohit pads it away. Paine appeals loudly, but even then it's too far out. Can't be given.
Behind a good length and outside the line of off stump, it's tapped down in front of covers from the back foot.
A rather stifled shout, but this is sliding down leg. Length ball on middle and leg, catches Agarwal on the pads as he misses his flick.
Good length delivery around the off stump, Mayank presents the full face as he blocks it down.
Coming in at first but then straightening off the seam, Agarwal is watchful as he turns this away past the short leg fielder.
On the pads once more, a length ball, Mayank goes deep inside the crease and blocks it down in front of short leg.

Comfortably done. Cummins bowls it on the pads and Rohit just tickles it down to fine leg for a single. The other batsmen got out trying to do this same thing, only Sharma has done it with full control.
Short and wide outside off, it's punched off the back foot to the covers for no run.
Quite full and loopy, around off, Mayank presses forward and works it away.
Agarwal moves inside the line and turns it with the spin on the leg side.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Too straight in line, a flatter ball, worked away on the leg side.

Safe! Agarwal survives. Rohit turns this off the back foot towards backward square leg and takes off. The fielder there throws it to Paine as Mayank slides in. An appeal is made when the bails are taken off and it goes upstairs. Replays show the opener is fine, but a direct hit would have made things interesting.
Hangs on the back foot again and defends it well.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman. Another dot.
Back of a length on off, Agarwal gets behind the line and defends.
Short of a good length around off, kept out off the back foot.

No hat-trick for Cummins, but it was mighty close though. Back of a length on the hips, Sharma swivels and pulls it past Marcus Harris at leg gully, who dives to his right but it just comes at him too fast. It goes through to fine leg and a single is taken.
Rohit Sharma to bat next.

OUT! Fourth wicket down and Pat Cummins has taken all of them. Is this a tired man? Doesn't look like it at all. He's breathing fire. Absolutely unreal. A bit of a soft dismissal though on this occasion. Back of a length down the leg side, Rahane looks to help the pull fine down the leg side but gets it off the glove. It's only a feather, but it's enough and Tim Paine behind dives to his left to take it. Not what you'd have expected, really. This is sensational. Cummins in on a hat-trick.
Agarwal goes on the back foot and tickles it fine down the leg side for a double.
Some serious turn for Lyon. He lands it on off and it spins a long way, goes down leg in fact as Agarwal misses his flick. A shout from Paine but nothing from it.
Goes with the spin as he turns it in front of short leg.
Loopy and quite full on leg, Mayank flicks it off his pads to short mid-wicket.
Rahane makes use of his feet to get off the mark. Dances down and eases it to long on for a single.
Tossed up off break on middle stump, Agarwal flicks it fine down the leg side and steals a quick single.
Ajinkya Rahane walks in at number 5, replacing his skipper.

OUT! An action replay of the Pujara dismissal. Cummins has his third! India's other in-form batsman has also been dismissed for nought. Believe me, Virat Kohli has a zero against his name. Just proves that he is human too. Length ball on the pads, just the plan and VK takes the bait. He flicks this in the air and Marcus Harris at backward square leg moves to his right and takes a good, low catch. Cummins has worked really hard in this series and especially in this match, and is reaping the rewards now. Three wickets in three overs so far. His figures read 3-2-2-3. A double-wicket maiden this. The Aussies are pumped up here, are they sensing a huge fightback? Nothing is impossible in this game and the visitors would know better, can't afford being complacent.
Angling at the pads, worked away towards the mid-wicket area.
Oooh! Another short length delivery that is hit slightly in the air. Kohli tries to fend it off on the leg side but the ball goes off the top half of his bat in the air towards short mid-wicket.
Length ball first up on middle, pushed towards to mid-wicket.
Drinks have been called for. Meanwhile, Virat Kohli walks into the middle at number 4, replacing Cheteshwar Pujara.

OUT! Gone second ball! Pujara has a rare duck! Caught at leg gully and Cummins has his second wicket in three deliveries. Length ball on the pads and it is instinctively flicked by Pujara towards the leg side. But lo and behold, there is Marcus Harris at leg gully taking an easy catch. Great bowling to the plan and good captaincy too. The first innings centurion has gone without troubling the scorers in the second. Two wickets lost in quick succession and the Aussies have something to smile about here.
Length ball on the off stump, Pujara pushes away his first ball towards mid-wicket.
Full and loopy outside off, it's driven to wide mid off. Maiden from Nathan Lyon.
Uses the depth of the crease again to block this out.
Quicker delivery just outside off, Mayank goes back and defends it under his nose.
Lyon lands it in the rough around outside off and it turns a long way. Agarwal comes forward to play as the ball takes the inside edge and goes past short leg.
Plants his front foot forward and drives it straight to the man at mid on.
Tossed up on off, spins in sharply, Agarwal drives but it takes the inside edge and goes past the leg stump.
Cheteshwar Pujara comes in at number 3.

OUT! Caught at gully. Great bouncer! Quick, at 141.2 kph, almost like the first innings dismissal. India lose their first one. Just as we were saying he was leaving the bouncers better this time around, he has made the same error as he did before. Short ball which gets big on the batsman, Vihari takes his eyes off and tries to fend it away. The ball goes off the shoulder of the bat and lobs up for one of the easiest catches to Khawaja at gully. Maiden wicket over for Cummins. India lead by 320.
Length ball outside off, pushed toward the mid off fielder.
Bouncer! Vihari sways out of the way and drops his hands down as he lets this one go. Good leave.
Short ball on off, Hanuma gets on top of the bounce as he defends the ball.
Fuller ball on the middle stump line, pushed towards mid on.
On the pads, Vihari turns it towards backward square leg.
Oooh! Draws Agarwal forward into the defense with a looped delivery on off stump, the ball takes the thick inside edge and rolls just away from the short leg fielder. Good bowling, this!
Going down the leg side with the turn, left alone.
Flatter ball on middle, the batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flatter on off, Vihari comes ahead and defends it on the off side. Quick single taken.

In the air but safe! Everything is going the way of the Indians here. The ball is beautifully looped up outside off and Agarwal, who is ahead to drive this one, is flummoxed by the flight and gets it on the thick inside half of the bat. The ball flies in the air but just away from the short mid-wicket fielder and Mayank escapes with a single.
Looped up on middle, defended onto the ground.
Change of ends for Nathan Lyon.
Another bumper to end the over, good technique from the batsman as he moves out of the way.
Fullish on a good length, Vihari times this well but straight to mid on.
Length ball on the pads, worked towards the backward square leg fielder.
Bouncer! Hanuma sways out of the way and lets it go.
Short ball, slightly slower. Agarwal jumps and keeps it down towards backward square leg for a run.
Starts off with a ball on the pads, worked away to mid-wicket by Vihari for a single.
Pat Cummins replaces Nathan Lyon.
Length ball on the pads, pushed away to mid-wicket.
Short ball outside off, Mayank gets on top of the ball and defends.
Outside off on this occasion, left alone.
Sliding down the leg side, Agarwal doesn't connect the flick.
Short ball on middle, worked away to fine leg for a single.
Length ball on off and middle, Vihari pushes this back down to mid on off the front foot.
Shortens the length on middle, Agarwal looks to flick it away but finds the fielder in the circle at square leg.
Flatter ball outside off, Mayank takes a stride ahead before defending.
Shorter and quicker outside off, pushed towards cover.
Flighted on off and turning in, the batsman comes down and smothers the spin on the ball.
Flatter ball outside off, Mayank comes ahead and dead-bats.
FOUR! Lofted over the mid on fielder and all the way to the fence. Flighted outside off, Agarwal hops down the track and scores a good boundary. Positive batting!
Length ball outside off, HV comes ahead and plays it onto the ground. Maiden over.
Length ball on middle, Vihari pushes it towards cover with an open face of the bat.
Another defense with the full face of the bat to this ball on middle.
Length ball, keeps a bit low. Vihari is also low and pushes it back to mid on.
Outside off, left alone by Hanuma.
Length ball on off and middle, Vihari stands tall and defends it back down to the bowler.
Short ball outside off and turning into Mayank, he steps back and pushes it towards cover off the back foot.
Flatter ball outside off. Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Flatter on off stump, pushed towards cover.

Oooh! Turn and bounce. The ball lands outside off and turns down to the leg stump. Agarwal tries to flick it but gets an inside edge onto the pad towards the leg side away from the fielder at short leg.
Flatter delivery on the pads, worked away to square leg for a single.
Appeal from the keeper down leg, but there is daylight between the bat and ball as it passes Vihari. Short and outside off and turns a long way to go down the leg side.
Nathan Lyon comes onto bowl, replacing Mitchell Starc.
At the hips for the last ball of the over, works it away to the deep square leg fielder for a single as he retains strike.
On a length and on off stump, Vihari comes ahead and defends it onto the ground.
Outside off and left alone by the batsman.
Short length ball on top of off, Vihari pushes it off the back foot towards cover.
Fuller this time and Hanuma has a big stride ahead before pushing it back down the ground to mid off.
Length ball outside off, Vihari defends it back down the ground.
Short length ball on middle, defended towards the bowler.
Another ball on middle and leg, Mayank pushes it towards mid-wicket.

FOUR! Freebies. The ball is on the hips and it is easily turned away fine on the leg side by Agarwal. Easy pickings for any Indian batsman this, who are usually very strong off their pads. Too fine for the fielder at the fence to come around and stop it.
Good bouncer! Just outside off, Agarwal ducks under the ball.
Angling down on the pads, worked away to the vacant square leg region. Three runs taken before the fine leg fielder can come around and throw back the ball.
Fuller length on off, Vihari comes ahead and drives this to mid on.
Well outside off on a length to end the over. Left alone by the batsman.
Length ball outside off, a front foot defensive stroke follows.
Short of a length on middle, pulled away by HV for a single to deep square leg.
Length ball outside off, Vihari plays a punchy shot towards cover for no run.
On a length outside off, keeps a tad low. Vihari does well to bring his bat down and keep it out towards mid on.
On the hips, Agarwal flicks it away to deep backward square leg for a single.
Sprayed wide down the leg side, the batsman can't reach it and Paine makes a good stop diving to his left.
Angling down on the hips this time, Hanuma works it away to backward square leg in the circle.
Another short ball in the line of off stump, Vihari gets on top of the bounce and defends this ball.
Fuller length coming in with the angle on off stump, pushed back down the ground on the front foot.
Short of a length, closer to the off stump now, Hanuma stands tall and defends it.
Around the wicket and wide outside off, Vihari looks to cut this away but pulls out of the shot at the last moment.
Length ball on top of off and middle, he is on his toes as he plays this towards mid on with an angled bat.
Short length ball outside off, the batsman pushes it away to cover off the back foot.
Length ball on off stump, Agarwal stays low and keeps it out towards mid off.
Going down leg once more, left alone.

FOUR! Lovely shot! Full and outside off, slightly swinging away. Mayank Agarwal, confident after his first dig, goes for a flowing cover drive and times it just good enough for it to reach the fence. Off the mark in style! The lead is 300 now!
Length ball angling down leg, Agarwal lets it go.
Josh Hazlewood to bowl from the other end.
Fullish in length and well outside off, Vihari looks to play at it but fails to connect.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for the batsman.
Hurled too far outside off, left alone.

FOUR! Streaky runs but Vihari will take it. Short and wide outside off, Hanuma throws his bat at it and gets it off the bottom edge between gully and the slip cordon. It races away to the third man fence for a boundary.
Angling away from around off, on a good length, it's left alone for the keeper to collect.
Full ball swinging in from around off, Vihari with a straight bat drives it to mid on.
